basic_info.title: An Ontological Model for Map Data in Automotive Systems
basic_info.venue: IEEE AIKE 2019 — 2nd IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Knowledge Engineering, Sardinia, Italy, June 3-5, 2019, pp. 140-147

method.notes: Investigates the feasibility of using OWL/RDF ontologies to model and process digital map data inside cars, where map data is a key source for perceiving the environment for advanced driver-assistance functions. Earliest/foundational paper of this BMW-Ulm ontological-map lineage.

gap_analysis.whats_missing: This work realizes the semantic-enrichment idea (thesis pillar P1b) SYMBOLICALLY via hand-authored OWL/RDF ontologies for in-car map representation, not as learned, vectorized graph tokens for a transformer encoder. It does not address GPS map matching or path prediction as a learning task and uses no sequence model, no latent-space RL, and no label-free training on raw fleet trajectories.
gap_analysis.novelty_note: A foundational symbolic/logical treatment of automotive map semantics that is orthogonal to the proposed learned-encoder + latent-RL + label-free-trajectory hybrid.

relevance.bmw_relevance: HIGH — the earliest, most-cited BMW in-house ontological map-data paper co-authored by the thesis interview lead Adel Ayara (with Glimm, Ulm University / BMW Car IT), foundational to the classical view of the P1b semantic-enrichment pillar.
